strengths.item: The paper is structurally organized in a recognizable ICLR-style format, with clear sectioning, numbered equations, figures, tables, and an appendix.
The main technical exposition appears generally readable, and equations on pages 4–6 are mostly well formatted and consistently numbered.
Most tables are legible with zoom, and captions generally connect the visual material to the surrounding discussion.

weaknesses.item: Pages 1–8 contain extensive red and blue inline text in the title, abstract, body, method descriptions, and tables, which looks like revision markup or highlighting and is highly distracting for a clean submission.
The title on page 1 is especially visually nonstandard: very large, bright red, small-caps, and hyphenated across lines, which harms the professional presentation.

Several figures are difficult to inspect at normal scale: Figure 1 on page 2 has very small internal labels, Figure 2 on page 3 is dense and compressed, and Figure 5 on page 8 has qualitative images that are too small for detailed visual verification.
Page 8 is visually crowded, containing multiple visual elements and a table, making inspection less comfortable.
Some captions are not fully self-contained, such as Figure 3, whose caption does not sufficiently explain why the highlighted pixels are considered unreliable.

dimension_review.evidence_summary: The PDF inspection found that the paper is broadly readable and organized, with an ICLR-like layout and mostly clear equations and tables. However, pages 1–8 show pervasive red/blue colored text, including the title and main body, creating a major formatting concern. Figures on pages 2, 3, 6, and 8 are generally relevant but often small, dense, or hard to inspect in detail; tables on pages 7–8 are mostly legible but compact.
dimension_review.rationale: The presentation is understandable but has notable visual and formatting issues that materially reduce ease of review. The organization and writing appear adequate, so this is not poor presentation, but the pervasive colored markup, nonstandard title formatting, small figure labels, and crowded visual pages go beyond minor polish issues. Therefore, the appropriate score is 2: fair presentation.
